scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: EMERGENCY!! The IT department is OFF THE NETWORK --
every single one of our 192.168.1.x machines, all at once, can't reach
anything!! Something around the switch box all our wires go into, switch0,
must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at switch0 and get us
back on the network -- the whole department is sitting here doing nothing!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket claimed every 192.168.1.x machine in the IT department was off the network and pointed a finger at switch0. A full SADE diagnostic sweep found no fault anywhere in the IT segment or the wider topology.

**Affected component:** None identified. All subsystems examined are healthy.

**Mechanism:** No outage mechanism exists. Switch0's bridge (br0) has both ports — eth0 (uplink to router0 via link_r0_sw0) and eth1 (downlink to lan_it) — in UP/forwarding state with zero errors, zero drops, and zero carrier-change events, ruling out any transient flap. Router0 holds a correctly populated routing table: 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24 as directly connected, with RIP-learned routes to every other subnet (192.168.3–4, 1.0.0.0/8, 128.168.0.0/16). No ACL or tc rules suppress IT traffic. No flap script or stress tool is running on any device.

**Localization:** It_hod, it_lab1, it_lab2, it_lab3, and it_lab4 all carry valid 192.168.1.x/24 addresses, reach the router0 gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and reach cross-segment destinations (e.g., office_pc at 192.168.3.2) with 0% loss. L2 identity is clean (no duplicate MACs). DHCP/link history shows no past lease losses or carrier events since container startup.

**Root cause:** There is no fault. The IT department network is fully operational and was so at time of inspection; the report could not be reproduced from any angle.

**Fix:** No corrective action required. Advise the ticket reporter to re-test; if a transient issue genuinely occurred prior to this investigation, no configuration change or service restart is warranted based on current evidence.
